```yaml
name: Release Please

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v2

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v2
        with:
          node-version: '14'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm install -g @googleapis/release-please-action

      - name: Run Release Please
        run: npx release-please --token ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }} --release-type simple --path . --target-branch main --config-file=.github/repo-release-please-config.json --manifest-file=.release-please-manifest.json --repo-url=https://github.com/openclaw-rocks/openclaw-operator.git --github-api-url=https://api.github.com --github-graphql-url=https://api.github.com/graphql --fork=false --include-component-in-tag=true --proxy-server=null --skip-github-release=false --skip-github-pull-request=false --skip-labeling=false
```

This workflow sets up a GitHub Actions job named "Release Please" that triggers on pushes to the `main` branch. It checks out the code, sets up Node.js, installs the necessary dependencies, and then runs the `release-please` command to create or update a release PR based on conventional commits. The `release-please` action handles updating the `CHANGELOG.md`, bumping the version in `Chart.yaml`, and creating a new tag when the release PR is merged.
